story_spine: A device that turns a census score into brake pressure ends up easing over public housing and going blank where nobody was counted.
opening_object_or_event: A 3D-printed box clamped to the front fork of a docked Citi Bike, with a wire running down to the brake arm.
reader_initial_state: That someone built a small machine which decides how hard a public hire bike is to pedal.
crip_turn: The easing over public housing and the unreadable block group are re-read as the same fact: the instrument can only pass on what the measure holds, so it is quietest where the pressure is least counted.
ending_move: The loose front-brake cables, found by hand on one bike in four, are the one thing the device turned up that no measure had a field for.

beats.why_reader_wants_next: A rider cannot feel the difference between a place under no pressure and a place nobody measured.

final_lens.lens_claim: An instrument that converts a classification into a force on the body can only transmit what the classification already carries: it eases where a remedy has already absorbed the pressure, and it has nothing to say at all about the places and people the survey never counted, so the ride is least informative exactly where the need is most acute.
final_lens.before_reading: A device that makes you feel the rent crisis in your legs.
final_lens.after_reading: A device that can only pass on what the measure holds, and is quietest where the pressure is least counted.
